rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No guess-before-reveal / predict-then-watch instruction pattern anywhere in the body — the file is a set-up-and-send-off exercise, not a demo beat. Scanned all 6 chunks for "guess"/"predict"/"before you watch" — none present.

Each chunk carries a self-carrying claim plus an actionable prompt: chunk 1 locates the transcript, chunk 2 pins the starting commit, chunk 3 states the push-is-optional default and reasoning, chunk 4 is the send-off directive itself, chunk 5 gives three concrete during-the-run behaviors (keep awake, nudge by hand, stop-if-off-rails). None is a bare wait-state bullet.

Closest candidate: chunk 1 header "Phase 1: Set the two return markers" (line 17) but chunk 1's own content only locates the transcript (marker 1 of 2) — marker 2 (the starting commit) lands in chunk 2 "Pin the starting point". This is a Phase-label header framing a multi-chunk phase (same pattern as sibling exercise walk-and-send-off.md, "Phase 1: Pick the task..." followed by a non-Phase sub-header "Push back until..."), and rule 15 explicitly exempts "Phase N:" headers from the claim-literal-truth bar (phase label, not a claim) — it stays inside. Other chunk headers ("Pin the starting point", "Push it only if you want it off this laptop", "While it runs") each match their own chunk's content directly.

Checked all five sub-items across chunks 0-5: no "Not X. Not Y. Z." construction; no anaphora/epistrophe triples; no self-grading superlative; no abstraction-noun stack; no verb-triplet-with-empty-leg. Closest candidate for "number + own retraction": chunk 5 line 56, "Past ten or so interventions, you have become the agent" — this stays inside because the shape the rule bans is a PRECISE number stated then immediately undermined by a retraction ("about 10%... could be more, could be less"); this line never states a precise number to retract — "or so" is baked-in vagueness from the start, matching the pacing-calibration carve-out this file's own maintainer block already invokes (check_pedagogy.md §16 boundary clause), not the rule-7 violation shape.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: chunk 5 "While it runs": line 53: "## While it runs" — this exercise's other four body headers are all imperative verbs (Set, Pin, Push, Send: lines 17, 28, 37, 45), matching rule 15's exercise-heading mandate (imperative or Phase label). "While it runs" is neither imperative nor a Phase label nor a declarative law-claim (it doesn't generalise past this task the way rule 15's two measured specimens do — close-the-ticket.md's "Anything can be reverse-engineered", fix-tests-first.md's "There is always a next plausible answer"); it's a bare temporal/context label. Harm: the mood-switch the rule protects (imperative-during-doing vs. declarative-at-the-generalising-beat) goes muted on this one slide — a reader can't tell from the header alone whether this chunk is still instructing or has shifted register, though the chunk's own bullets (imperative-adjacent: "Keep the laptop awake", "Nudge by hand") make the content itself unambiguous once read. A writing-class judge separately flagged this same header for lacking a command verb (noted in dispatch context); this is the matching slides-class finding on the same string, evaluated against rule 15's grammar-split concern rather than word-choice.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Recast as imperative to match its four siblings (e.g. a verb-first header naming what the student does during the run) — narrow lens only, not a rewrite.
